rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-1: about 38% of private employees lack paid leave usable for illness, so the term binds for them.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-2: most bound employers comply: payroll vendors build in accrual, and some workers complain.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-3: money wages are fixed in the short run by pay scales, annual raises and collective agreements.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-5: wages above the minimum can adjust over the medium horizon, as raises are set.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-6: for the marginal worker and employer, the term is worth less to the worker than it costs the employer.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-22: workers' alternatives to bound employment are clearly worse than employers' alternatives.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-24: labor-intensive businesses are valued on expected earnings.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-14: small-business and restaurant associations can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-14: unions can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-7: the minimum wage binds for some uncovered workers.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-9: employers can infer expected use of sick time from what they see of applicants.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-12: some existing PTO policies do not meet the conditions of use.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-8: employers can move hours between part-time and full-time staff.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-4: some uncovered workers would have worked while ill, or will use paid hours for other ends.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-26: some uncovered workers would have taken unpaid absences for illness without the Act.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-19: shift-based employers cover absent shifts, partly through agencies and on-call staff.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-17: most competitors of local service sellers are bound too.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-18: Varrow's tradable producers compete with Pellam producers, who are not bound.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-13: compliant and small firms compete in product markets with uncovered firms.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-11: the classification test is weakly enforced in some occupations, so contractor arrangements are open to some employers.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-15: some job changes are marginal enough that losing a balance and waiting 90 days decides them.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-16: complaints are unlikely for some workers.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-21: complaints are filed in meaningful numbers.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-029 (illustrative figures), A-10: some firms near six employees value staying exempt more than an extra hire.
